name: Son Bunyola
positioning: A restored 16th-century finca on a coastal estate in Mallorca's UNESCO-listed Tramuntana Mountains, with three standalone villas
best_for: Travelers who want a historic country estate with sea and mountain views
Hikers and cyclists exploring the Tramuntana Mountains
Groups wanting a private villa with its own pool

facts.text: Son Bunyola is on Mallorca's north-west coast in the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Tramuntana Mountains.
The hotel is set in a 16th-century finca, or manor house, at the heart of the estate.
The restoration was done with Mallorcan architects Gras Reynes Architecture Studio and interior designer Rialto Living, using traditional and local materials.
Some suites have private terraces with sweeping views.
The estate includes three standalone villas: Sa Punta de S'Aguila, Sa Terra Rotja and Son Balagueret, which can be hired year-round.
Son Balagueret villa has a 13th-century turret and a central courtyard.
Guests can swim in the pool and do yoga and tennis, and the mountain landscape suits hiking and cycling.
From the pebble beach below the hotel, guests can swim, kayak and picnic.
Sa Terrassa serves Mediterranean cuisine with sea views.
Mallorcan dishes are made from produce grown in the estate's gardens and orchards.
Son Bunyola was awarded a MICHELIN Key by The MICHELIN Guide in 2025 and 2026.
One bedroom, Room 1, is designed for wheelchair users.

highlights.text: The estate has three miles of unspoilt coastline, with olive groves and vineyards.
The original towers of the main house have been turned into two Tower Suites with vineyard and mountain views.
The terrace looks down over a small village to the bay and the Sa Foradada rock formation.
The pool sits on the historic terrace, and the former olive press has been restored.
Sa Punta de S'Aguila villa is built into the landscape in traditional Mallorcan style, with panoramic sea and mountain views.

considerations.text: The spa is small, run by locally based Gaia Natural Products, with a short menu of treatments using island oils.
There are not a lot of facilities for children, though there is a smaller pool by the main one.
WhataHotel notes the remote mountain location requires a car for exploring.
